newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's budget deficit may exceed 4 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Israel's budget deficit may exceed 4 pct of GDP.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Tuesday that the latest tax revenue figures indicate that Israel's 1996 budget deficit may exceed four percent of gross domestic product.
The government had targeted this year's deficit at 2.5 percent of GDP. As recently as Monday Treasury officials were saying the deficit would be about 3.5 percent.
In a speech to rally coalition legislators to support the Treasury embattled 1997 budget, Meridor said passage of the spending package this month was a test of the government's ability to lead.
The budget deficit target for 1997 is 2.8 percent of GDP.
"The current government has not been given such an important test," he told members of parliament.

Meridor is facing strong opposition to the budget package, which in its final form will contain approximately seven billion shekels in spending cuts. Opponents, including many coalition legislators, say the burden of the cuts will fall on lower-income groups.

Meanwhile, a group of academic economists warned Meridor on Tuesday against raising taxes as a substitute for spending cuts next year. They were especially critical of proposals to reduce subsidies to employers' social security contributions.
They also warned against cuts in capital spending and research and development.

Treasury officials are in the midst of preparing a second round of budget cuts that could reach as high as 2.3 billion shekels. These come on top of the 4.9 billion shekel reductions contained in the original 1997 budget presented to parliament.
The exact size of the cuts is expected to be announced as early as Wednesday.
